svg.text: Guidemen rebuild — capture harness fixed, and what it revealed
2026-09-18 · first visual verification after five passes of geometry-only work
The harness that finally works
SceneCapture2D
-> persistent TextureRenderTarget2D
-> read_render_target(world, rt, True)
-> binary PPM written from the editor
-> PNG converted outside the editor
Three things had to be learned:
· export_render_target writes nothing in this build
· the editor Python has no numpy and no PIL
· set_visibility does not affect traces; collision does
Immediately exposed: two buildings
Every capture was showing TWO overlapping Guidemen actors — a stale
BP_Guidemen_V5_4K_C_0 left by an earlier staged setup, plus the current
one. The level held 16 actors. This contaminated every image and would
have made any material or geometry diagnosis wrong.
Cleaned: 16 stray actors removed, level now zero.
The staged harness leaves actors in the world by design, so a leaked
setup is silent and poisons every later capture. Always list the level
actors before trusting an image.
Materials rebuilt — 47 slots
Most of the building rendered saturated blue with relief: a normal map
read as base colour. Only the two materials rebuilt in the earlier pass
(stone, tile) rendered correctly — which was the tell.
BaseColor -> BaseColor (sRGB)
Normal -> Normal (non-sRGB)
MetallicRoughness.G -> Roughness
MetallicRoughness.B -> Metallic
AO.R -> Ambient Occlusion
Ten *_Rebuild20260918 materials; old graphs kept for rollback.
Checked before blaming the materials
M_AgedTimber_BaseColor.jpg RGB (0.397, 0.249, 0.157) brown
M_GrayClayTile_BaseColor.jpg RGB (0.236, 0.243, 0.232) grey
M_AgedTimber_Normal.jpg RGB (0.498, 0.498, 0.988) proper normal map
Imported UE textures are correct too:
BaseColor TC_DEFAULT sRGB on 4096x4096
Normal TC_NORMALMAP sRGB off 4096x4096
MetallicRoughness TC_MASKS sRGB off 4096x4096
AO TC_MASKS sRGB off 4096x4096
So the source art and the import are both sound.
The roof reads correctly from above
The top-down view shows a clean hip-roof plan: the ridge along X with the
four hip lines running diagonally to the corners.
The X / bowtie pattern is the hip lines, not a valley.
That is exactly what a 庑殿 roof looks like from directly overhead, and it
agrees with the measurement that every shell falls monotonically away from
the ridge.
Tiles match the source to the centimetre; the source's own shell defect
remains corrected at 9.89 / 9.86 cm clearance under the tile tops.
Still open — the blue timber and doors
With a single actor and fully rebuilt materials, the timber, columns and gate doors still render saturated blue. Ruled out:
material wiring all ten rebuilt with correct channels | source maps correct albedo and normals
imported textures sRGB, compression and sizes all correct | stale actor level cleaned, defect persists
And the contradiction worth chasing: with a flat mid-grey material on all 47 slots, the stone, roof and crenellations went grey while the timber
stayed blue — which points at those meshes rather than their materials, most likely vertex colour or a per-mesh override.
Where this leaves the rebuild
Fixed: the capture harness, the level contamination, the ten materials (47 slots rebound, rollback graphs intact). Verified: the assembly is a faithful copy of
the source (18,820 of 18,822 instances within 1 cm), and the roof reads correctly from above. Open: the blue timber, now cheap to isolate — with the harness
working, hiding component groups by collision will name the blue geometry outright instead of inferring it.
